decided: To tell whether a commit is needed, orbit compares the user's files with the last commit using a throwaway copy of git's index in the system's temporary folder, so the check never writes anything in the user's repository.
alternatives: compare each file's content one at a time, which misjudges links between files and files git converts on the way in
let the comparison update git's index in place and say so in the promise that orbit's pull-request commands only read
why: Orbit's pull-request commands promise to read and print, never to write in the repository. A comparison on git's own index quietly rewrites it; the copy keeps the promise while git still makes the comparison exactly as it would for a real commit.

relies_on.title: The `orbit pr` command observes and prints; it never writes

defines.definition: the file in which git records the versions of files staged for the next commit, and when it last looked at each
